story: Lakshmi rose from the churning of the ocean of milk, seated on a lotus, and chose Vishnu as her husband. She joins him in every avatar: as Sita beside Rama and as Rukmini beside Krishna.
belief: Devotees pray to her for wealth, health, beauty and good fortune, and believe she stays only in clean, honest and hard-working homes. On Diwali night, lamps are lit so she can find her way in.
turns: She is called chanchala, 'restless', because she leaves those who grow arrogant or lazy. When Indra disrespected a garland given by the sage Durvasa, she left heaven itself, and the gods lost their fortune until the ocean was churned.
facts: The Ashtalakshmi are her eight forms, from the wealth of grain to courage and knowledge.
Her vahana, the owl, is read as a warning not to be blinded by wealth.
The gold coins pouring from her hand stand for prosperity flowing to her devotees.
